title: Best Practices for Reducing Power Consumption on STM32 MCUs
content:
Hello everyone,

I'm working on a battery-powered STM32 project and would like to improve its power efficiency without sacrificing performance.

I'm interested in learning from developers who have hands-on experience with STM32 devices:

  • Which low-power mode do you use most often?

  • What techniques have made the biggest difference in extending battery life?

  • Are there any common mistakes to avoid when configuring clocks, peripherals, or wake-up sources?

  • Which debugging tools or profiling methods do you recommend for measuring actual power consumption?

I'd appreciate any practical tips, examples, or resources that have worked well in real-world projects.

Thanks in advance for your insights!

scraped_replies.html:
Hello ​@devillier44850 

So we can better help you, could you please specify which STM32 MCU H7 product you are planning to use? Each one has its own characteristics.

Also, could you describe the project you want to develop? Does it include wireless technology, for example a Bluetooth module or a LoRa module? This may affect the MCU choice.

Each low-power mode has its own use case, and there is no single mode that is used most often. The most suitable mode depends on your application.

To avoid common mistakes, you can consult the WIKI and this article that will help you build basic knowledge about using low-power modes.

You can also run a few tests using those examples to see the power consumption of your system, including both software and hardware. You can measure the actual power consumption using various methods:

  • a standard multimeter
  • an X-NUCLEO-LPMA1 in standalone mode or with CubeMonitor-Power

There are resources explaining how to use them. If you are interested, just let me know and I will provide the links.
BR
Gyessine
